Why this check matters: neither `tsc` nor `vitest` (jsdom) can compute real flex-wrap, real text-metric wrapping, or real cross-element geometry — jsdom reports every bounding rect as 0. This component introduces genuinely long English fallback copy (e.g. the location variant's body: "You're currently shopping on {currentStore}. Switch to {targetStore} for local pricing, currency and shipping options.", rendered in the story with "Zimmermann Australia"/"Zimmermann Germany" substituted in) inside a narrow drawer. The drawer's `size="prompt"` variant (added in an earlier, already-committed step, in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts`) has a `min-width: 25.125rem` (402px) floor above the `md` breakpoint (`48em` = 768px, defined in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts`), full-width/auto-height below it. The new component's own recipe (`zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts`) applies `padding: var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (24px) on all sides of `root`, a `gap` between content and button-group that is `var(--zimm-scale-4xl)` (64px) below `md` and `var(--zimm-scale-5xl)` (80px) at/above `md`, and a `var(--zimm-scale-m)` (16px) gap between the two stacked CTA buttons in `buttonGroup`. Both CTAs are `ZimmButton size="adaptive"` (40px tall below `md`, 52px at/above `md`, per `zimmButton/index.tsx`'s own doc comment).

Important: `index.stories.tsx` has NO decorator wrapping the component at a fixed width — so a real browser viewport resize should genuinely reach the component's own `@media (min-width: 48em)` rules, unlike a fixed-width `Box` decorator which cannot respond to a real viewport. This means a live Playwright check against the actual Storybook dev server CAN prove the responsive claims above, if you get the setup right.

Do this:

1. Check if port 6006 is already in use (`lsof -i :6006` or similar). If free, start Storybook in the background: `npm run storybook` (defined in package.json as `storybook dev -p 6006`), with a reasonable startup timeout (60-90s) — do NOT run `npm start`, only `npm run storybook`. If it fails to start or times out, say so explicitly and report this whole angle as unable-to-verify rather than fabricating numbers — do not guess at layout values.

2. Once Storybook is up, find the real story IDs for this component (fetch `http://localhost:6006/index.json` or `http://localhost:6006/stories.json` and grep for "ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch", or check the sidebar) — the title is `Layout/ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` with named exports `Location` and `Language`, so the ID is likely `layout-zimmcountrylanguagemismatch--location` / `--language`, but confirm the real ID rather than assuming.

3. Using Playwright (`@playwright/test` is installed — you can write a small throwaway `.mjs`/`.ts` script using the `playwright` package directly, run with `node`, and delete it afterward, or use `npx playwright` ad hoc — your choice, just don't leave any new file behind in the repo when you're done), for EACH of the two stories, load the iframe URL directly (`http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story`) at each of these real viewport widths: 375px (mobile), 402px (the prompt-size floor), 768px (the `md` breakpoint itself), and 1440px (desktop). At each width, measure and record:
   - `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` vs the viewport width (any horizontal overflow at all is a real defect).
   - The drawer panel's own `getBoundingClientRect()` width.
   - The heading, body paragraph, and button-group container's `getBoundingClientRect()`s — confirm no clipping (text isn't cut off, nothing overflows its parent), and confirm the two buttons render in a vertical stack (not overlapping, not side-by-side) with a real measured gap between their two rects.
   - The root container's computed `padding` (via `getComputedStyle`) — confirm it's actually ~24px on each side at every width tested.
   - The gap between the content block (heading+body) and the button group — confirm it measures ~64px below 768px and ~80px at/above 768px (measure the real pixel gap between the content block's bottom edge and the button group's top edge, don't just trust the CSS source).
   - Each button's own rendered height — confirm ~40px below 768px and ~52px at/above 768px.
   Do this for BOTH the Location and Language stories (Language's body text is shorter, Location's is the longest — if only one shows a real problem, say which).

4. Stop the Storybook server when done (kill the background process).

5. Produce a "visual checkpoint brief" table for a human reviewer (Marcel) with one row per measurable property per state/width, in this exact format:

| What to check | Figma node | Expected value | How to verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| ... | ... | ... | ... |
